item.description: Nowhere To Run There don't appear to be many safe havens as the situation in Middle East continues to evolve. Not in markets, and not in the region either. item.title: Pakistan-Afghanistan Conflict Halts Critical Central Asian Trade Routes
item.description: Largely overlooked because of the burgeoning conflict in the Middle East, “open war” has erupted between Pakistan and Afghanistan’s Taliban leadership. The fighting all along its southern rim represents a major setback for Central Asia’s global trade agenda. The Pakistani-Afghan conflict shows no signs of easing after almost a week of fighting. item.title: Strait of Hormuz Closure Sends European Gas Benchmark Soaring
item.description: Military strikes in the Middle East and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz have triggered one of the sharpest moves in European gas markets over the past year, with the Title Transfer Facility (TTF) benchmark surging on disrupted liquefied natural gas (LNG) flows. The shock is transmitting directly into European power markets, with price reactions varying according to national gas exposure. item.title: The Dark Horse That Could Deliver the World's First Fusion Reactor
item.description: The race is on to achieve commercial nuclear fusion. item.title: Iran War Upends LNG Market and Jolts Gas Prices
item.description: Just a month ago, Europe was attracting most LNG spot cargoes as solid demand and fast-depleting gas inventories fetched higher prices than in Asia, where demand was lackluster. A month is a long time in today’s geopolitical order and this week the global gas market was jolted into a massive shock that upended supply and demand trends. item.title: Tanker Squeeze Adds Insult to Oil Injury amid Iran War
item.description: Tanker rates are through the roof, movement through the Strait of Hormuz is severely reduced because of war cover cancellations by insurers, and the combination of these developments has sent oil prices flying. Now, there’s a third factor that would likely aggravate the situation further: there are not enough supertankers.
